summary: The note describes a community movement to make technology education accessible across ages, genders and languages, sparked by a September 15, 2023 community board meeting. It profiles leaders and programs such as TechBridge, ElderConnect, CodeGirl and TechLingo, along with a young robotics mentor. It closes with plans to partner with tech companies for internships and to pursue grants and scholarships.
one_line: Local leaders and programs like TechBridge, ElderConnect, CodeGirl and TechLingo are expanding inclusive tech education to close the community's digital divide.
key_facts: The movement began at a community board meeting on September 15, 2023, where local educators and tech professionals voiced concerns about the growing digital divide.
Martina Gonzales, a former computer science professor, founded TechBridge, a grassroots initiative to democratize access to technology education.
TechBridge started with free weekend coding boot camps for youngsters and introductory tech talks for adults.
Jonathan O’Neil is Director of ElderConnect, a program that empowers seniors with digital skills; it hosts weekly get-togethers on online banking and telemedicine appointments.
O’Neil said, "In today's culture, if you aren't online, you're practically invisible."
ElderConnect's volunteers often include tech-savvy teenagers, creating intergenerational exchange where kids and seniors learn from each other.
Aditi Singh, an 18-year-old high school graduate, mentors elementary students in robotics and AI and runs a bimonthly robotics workshop at the community library.
Rachel Morrison leads CodeGirl, which began as after-school programs and expanded to offer scholarships for girls to attend tech conferences and join high-level coding competitions.
Damian Rodriguez, a language educator and software developer, launched TechLingo in November 2023, offering tech classes in both English and Spanish.
Michaela Chu, a local entrepreneur and benefactor of TechBridge, says tech skills foster innovation and help the community thrive in a digital economy.
Reported ripple effects include local businesses seeing more qualified job applicants and schools introducing more advanced tech courses.
Future goals include partnering with tech giants for internships and job shadowing, and exploring grants and scholarships for further education.
Community centers, libraries, schools and cafes became hubs for tech education.
